summary: Chat sessions show prolonged priming and delayed first tokens after kernel optimizer rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovusWallet, dedicated) reports a noticeable increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for short-chat completions (priming/initial message) starting immediately after the kernel optimizer hotfix (runtime v2.4.7 -> 2.4.8) and a compiler micro-optimization merged on 2026-03-09. The effect is most visible on small payload chats (<= 80 tokens) and impacts both streaming and non-streaming completion endpoints.

Impact:
- Customer reports degraded UX: single-turn quick replies take 2.5–4s longer to produce the first token vs baseline.
- Error rates are slightly elevated for streaming sessions (intermittent 504s during slow priming).
- Affects dedicated cluster for NovusWallet and appears in us-east and us-west pools.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: nv-rt-dedicated-42 (prod, us-east-1)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v2.4.8 (kernel optimizer + scheduler affinity change)
- Compiler: inference-compiler v1.9.3 (micro-optimizations merged 2026-03-09)
- Models: redwood-13B-quant (pinned by customer), open-13B-compat fallback policy

Steps to reproduce (from support runbook):
1. Open new chat session against customer-dedicated endpoint with small prompt (20–60 tokens).
2. Measure time from POST /v1/chat/completions to first token chunk on streaming socket and first token payload on non-streaming.
3. Compare TTFB distribution to baseline snapshot from 2026-03-08.

Observed behavior:
- Median TTFB increased from ~120ms to ~450ms for small prompts; p95 spiked from ~380ms to ~1.2s.
- Intermittent 504s observed when priming overlaps autoscaler scale-up events.
- Tracing shows an extra 200–600ms in the pre-inference stage (handshake/allocator + KV cache warm checks).

Expected behavior:
- TTFB should remain within historical SLO (median <200ms for small prompts on dedicated pools).

Logs/metrics attached:
- Traces: trace IDs: trace-20260310-us-east-99a, trace-20260312-us-west-21b (links above in comments).
- Console dashboard snapshots (ttfb_heatmap_2026-03-09.png, ttfb_heatmap_2026-03-11.png).

Initial hypothesis:
1) Kernel optimizer introduced a fast-path selector that falls back to a slower compatibility execution path for certain quantized parameter layouts (affects first-token generation where KV cache validation occurs).
2) Scheduler affinity change increased preemption and caused short-lived allocation waits for small, latency-sensitive requests.
3) Autoscaler interaction: new kernel delays combined with scale events cause transient 504s when priming competes with scale-up CPU/GPU binding.

Investigation summary:
- Replayed customer traces on staging with and without the kernel optimizer flag; reproduced ~300ms regression on first token when optimizer enabled for redwood-13B-quant.
- Heap and allocator logs show an additional 150–400ms spent in "KV cache validation" codepath when optimizer selector triggers.
- Scheduler team confirms affinity reshuffle landed in v2.4.8 and increased short-request queue wait under bursty traffic in dedicated pools.

Current actions in progress:
- Rolling a targeted rollback of the optimizer selector on the NovusWallet dedicated pool (canary nodes) to validate regression removal.
- Adding a temporary route rule to pin small/prompt-size requests to nodes with older kernels while fix is validated.
- Engineering to add telemetry to flag when the slow compatibility path is taken (metrics emitted by compiler).

Follow-up / Next steps:
- If rollback on canary removes regression, schedule global rollback for impacted pools and fast-track a patched optimizer that avoids the compatibility fallback for quantified KV layouts.
- Add a scheduler tuning knob to reduce preemption for latency-sensitive small requests during autoscale.
- Customer-facing: provide NovusWallet an interim mitigation (route pinning) and credit for degraded UX during incident window.

Resolution: In progress — mitigation and telemetry changes being validated on canary as of 2026-03-14.

investigation_notes: Reproduce steps isolating the compiler optimizer flag show consistent first-token penalty for quantized model layouts. The compatibility kernel path performs additional memory layout validation and a slower matmul kernel that has higher setup cost per invocation. Scheduler preemption exacerbates this by delaying the priming request until a less optimal core/GPU binding is available. Combined effect explains observed 500–800ms regressions in worst cases.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: canary rollback + traffic pinning. Engineering patch to optimizer guard expected within 48 hours of 2026-03-14. No permanent rollback globally yet; will coordinate with release manager after patch validation.
follow_up_actions: 1) Merge optimizer guard (runtime PR) and land patched release. 2) Deploy scheduler affinity override for dedicated pools. 3) Create a postmortem documenting the kernel selector test coverage gap and add a preflight ttfb regression dashboard to the rollout playbook. 4) Issue customer credit and hold an incident review with NovusWallet.
